items.title: Magnarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2010
items.q: I just ear train by listening to Sonny Rollins and trying to hear what he did in the 60’s

ctx.x: I think you can get arrested for that. Transcribing while driving.

Well transcribing, what I mean by that, just to clarify, I just ear train. And I ear train by listening to Sonny Rollins and trying to hear what he did in the 60’s or Ornette Coleman. I try to diversify, you know, don’t just stay with one kind of music. Sometimes I’ll listen to Bach partitas or 18 bars of Mozart or something. Just try to develop your ear that way. That’s what I’m talking about.

Do you ever get students now that come in knowing more than you do about the theory of jazz, or stuff that they’ve learned. They may have a high school teacher who went to music college for jazz and they have imparted things to them that you’re not familiar with. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -3-
